neighbours.label: the thought/speech verb of an attribution tag placed after the reported clause ('..., she thought,'); the same verbs leading a sentence or reporting plain speech stay low
fire: It was far too late to turn back now, he thought, and kept walking.
The whole plan was ridiculous, she decided, but she signed anyway.
Nobody in the village would ever believe him, the old man thought.
This is the worst storm in years, Tom muttered, and shut the window.
Maybe the letter had never arrived at all, she wondered, staring at the gate.
The house looked smaller than he remembered, he thought, as the taxi stopped.
Somebody must have taken the keys, Anna reasoned, because the drawer was empty.
They would laugh at her tomorrow, she felt, no matter what she said.
quiet: He thought it was far too late to turn back now, and kept walking.
She decided the whole plan was ridiculous, but she signed anyway.
The old man knew that nobody in the village would ever believe him.
Tom shut the window because the storm was the worst in years.
Staring at the gate, she asked whether the letter had ever arrived.
As the taxi stopped, the house looked smaller than before.
Anna found the drawer empty because somebody had taken the keys.
No matter what she said, they would laugh at her tomorrow.
